title: What does a CRM cost per user each month: HubSpot, monday CRM, Zoho CRM, Pipedrive or Salesforce?
text:
Summary

For annual billing, HubSpot's Starter Customer Platform offer is $7 per seat per month, monday CRM Basic is $12, Zoho CRM Standard $14 and Pipedrive Lite $14; Salesforce Starter Suite is $25 per user per month with monthly or annual billing. For five paid users, those rates give annual subscription totals of $420, $720, $840, $840 and $1,500 before tax, subject to the offer and seat conditions below. Zoho CRM is also free for up to 3 users.

...

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HubSpot Starter Customer Platform | $7 annually; $10 monthly | $420 on annual offer | New customers, limited-time offer; 2026-11-02 |
| monday CRM Basic | $12 annually; $18 monthly | $720 for five paid seats | USD rates checked 2026-08-17; published five-seat group |
| Pipedrive Lite | $14 annually | $840 | One annual payment; 2026-11-02 |
| Salesforce Starter Suite | $25, monthly or annually | $1,500 over a year | Payment schedule depends on choice; 2026-11-02 |
| Zoho CRM Standard | $14 annually; $20 monthly | $840 | US-dollar list price; 2026-11-08 |
| Zoho CRM Free | $0, up to 3 users | Not a five-user plan | Free user limit checked 2026-11-02 |

Scroll sideways to see every column.

The annual totals assume five paid seats throughout the year. Pipedrive's annual rate means $168 per seat paid for the year, so $168 x 5 = $840. At Salesforce's monthly Starter rate, five users cost $25 x 5 = $125 each month; $1,500 is twelve months of that spending, rather than the amount due at signup on monthly billing.

HubSpot's bundle offer requires "upfront payment and annual commitment" at the $7 rate. Five seats therefore mean $7 x 5 x 12 = $420 before tax at signup. The bundle and Sales Hub Starter are different purchase options: do not assume that an offer for one automatically applies to the other.

The monday figures are the dated USD rates in the table. Confirm the current US-dollar checkout total before committing, including how many paid seats your team must buy. Zoho's paid editions run Standard at $14, Professional at $23, Enterprise at $40 and Ultimate at $52 per user per month billed annually, or $20, $35, $50 and $65 month to month (Zoho CRM pricing, US-dollar prices checked 2026-11-08).

...

monday sells paid subscriptions in seat groups, with a minimum of 3 seats. Its help article gives the example of four people needing five seats. A two-person team using the dated Basic annual rate would therefore pay $12 x 3 x 12 = $432, even though only two people need logins.

The published seat schedule starts at three and then rises in multiples of five, so five people fit a five-seat group and a sixth requires ten seats. Confirm the CRM order follows that schedule before adding someone. The new headcount can increase the bill by a group of seats rather than just one person.

...

Pipedrive Growth costs $39 per seat per month billed annually, checked 2026-11-02. Its annual payment is $468 per seat, or $468 x 5 = $2,340 for five seats. Compared with Lite's $840 total, the extra $1,500 buys access to features including email synchronization and follow-up automations; those are useful comparison points if manual follow-ups are the reason for moving.

Salesforce Pro Suite is $100 per user per month billed annually, checked 2026-11-02. Five users mean $100 x 5 x 12 = $6,000 for the annual subscription. Sales quoting and forecasting are listed with Pro Suite, so a team needing those tools should compare that edition rather than budgeting from Starter's headline price.

title: CRM pricing comparison in 2026: What six vendors' sticker ...
text:
## Seat floors and ladders that bill for logins nobody uses

Two of the six vendors here do not let you buy exactly the number of seats your team has. Not even close, in one case.

monday CRM sells seats in fixed steps: 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50. There is no 4. Nothing between 30 and 40, either. 

A six person team buys 10 seats. A thirty two person team buys 40. 

monday's own support content describes the ladder as growing "in multiples of 5," which holds up to 30 seats and then breaks on the next rung.

Close CRM has the opposite shape of problem. Solo is capped at exactly one user, so the moment a second person joins, the plan jumps straight to Essentials, nearly four times the per seat rate on annual billing, with no smaller team tier in between.

HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, and Zoho CRM all bill per actual seat with no floor. 

HubSpot has a different forced cost mechanic instead: cross your marketing contact limit by even one record and the account upgrades to the next contact tier automatically, at midnight, and stays billed there until renewal, per HubSpot's own support documentation. No warning either.

...

Across these six vendors, a workable paid seat runs from $9 (Close Solo, capped at one user) to $28 (monday CRM Pro) before AI usage, add ons, or onboarding. Salesforce starts higher. Its entry seat is $25, and its highest tier reaches $550.
